records.statement: Heading 'Another Judgment' begins different sign-type rules for locating lost objects or beasts.
preconditions: Source switches technique; do not silently merge with lunar-ruler method.

records.statement: Common signs refer to within house for inanimate objects, but to watery or market/rushy areas for living beasts.
preconditions: Different place inference for dead things versus livestock; ambiguous exact sign glyphs.

records.statement: Fixed signs are read as property hidden near ground, inside walls or hollow trees.
preconditions: Not a universal sign-to-location invariant across preceding methods.

records.statement: Movable signs are interpreted as high roofs/ceilings; watery signs as under water or foundations.
preconditions: Original sign categories intersect; not necessarily mutually exclusive.

records.statement: Sixth lord unfortunate by Saturn or Mars and cadent suggests beasts lost or stolen.
preconditions: Keep planetary affliction and sixth-ruler house status.

records.statement: Another planet separating from Moon's house-lord or second lord suggests beasts carried away; absence of separations suggests not far.
preconditions: Reverse separating planet is what purportedly indicates outside actor.

records.statement: Moon or Moon-house lord applying to eighth, or beast significator occupying eighth under adverse square from infortune, alleges animal death.
preconditions: Alternative death signs; no historical animal outcome.

records.statement: Lord of sixth or twelfth in ninth/tenth may imply cattle with officer/keeper, bailiff or constable.
preconditions: Legal custody is an unverified authorial conclusion.

records.statement: Sixth or twelfth lord in its own respective house means animals held in a close pound or secured place.
preconditions: Two distinct house-lord conditions.

records.statement: Sixth lord favoured by Jupiter or Venus while in second, sixth or eleventh gives a claim of eventual recovery.
preconditions: Specific fortune plus placement conditions.

records.statement: Lunar term lord or fourth-cusp ruler joined to first ruler provides another favourable cattle-recovery indication.
preconditions: Historical term/cusp method; require source-defined rulership.

records.statement: Sixth or twelfth lord in a trine to Sun outside angles is separately interpreted as return.
preconditions: Exact trine-to-Sun source glyph; tentative if image printer unclear.

records.statement: Heading 'How far off a thing lost is from the owner' introduces angular-quarter distance method.
preconditions: Distinct from subsequent livestock location methods.

records.statement: Moon in same quarter as first lord and at most one sign apart means lost thing in owner's house or immediately near.
preconditions: Required same zodiac quarter; one sign may be approximately thirty degrees.

records.statement: More than thirty through seventy degrees within same relative quarter is said to locate property somewhere in owner's town.
preconditions: This source degree range is not a measured town radius.

records.statement: When Moon and first ruler are beyond ninety-degree same-quadrant condition, source describes object as far away.
preconditions: Distance cutoffs approximate; other adjacent methods assign different units.

records.statement: A separate 'Beasts stolen or strayed' heading begins sign-class test based on Moon's house lord or second lord.
preconditions: This is distinct from previous generic property direction.

records.statement: When lunar domicile lord or second lord separates from its own domicile and missing goods are fixed, it is called stolen.
preconditions: Source's fixed/movable distinction applies to goods category and may be typographically ambiguous.

records.statement: If the object is movable/live beast under analogous separation, it is said to have fled on its own.
preconditions: The same separation is interpreted differently by object type.

records.statement: Sixth lord angular suggests beasts confined in enclosed places, cadent moving away, succedent nearby pasture.
preconditions: All three modalities of houses retained separately.

records.statement: Sixth lord in fiery sign suggests eastward woods/burnt brush; angular fiery adds enclosures.
preconditions: Both sign element and angular status modify place.

records.statement: Sixth lord in earth signs suggests dry southern ground, and in angle enclosed pound or mud wall.
preconditions: Additional succedent status means closer right-hand place.

records.statement: Sixth lord in airy sign is associated with open flat land to west; angular enclosed or succedent right/west.
preconditions: Historical geography, no real-world coordinates.

records.statement: Sixth lord in watery sign suggests northern low ground, water meadows or place where cattle watered.
preconditions: House angle/succedent/cadent further affects proximity/direction.

records.statement: Heading 'In what ground they be' introduces terrain from modality of sixth lord.
preconditions: Distinguish soil/terrain from cattle-custody or recovery.

records.statement: Sixth lord in movable signs suggests hilly ground.
preconditions: Source-specific modality association, not universal.

records.statement: Sixth lord in fixed signs suggests plain ground/new building/newly ploughed fields.
preconditions: The printed source contrasts with other fixed-sign hiding-low rule.

records.statement: Common signs suggest wet, rushy and ditch-filled ground.
preconditions: No measured physical place.

records.statement: Moon term lord in fixed/movable/common signs supplies separate terrain rules: plain or new building, new lands/hills, rushy watery pits.
preconditions: This is TERM lord, not sixth lord; another hierarchy of significators.

records.statement: Heading 'The Cattle shall to Pound' gives Moon in twelfth or afflicted by twelfth lord as custody conditions.
preconditions: Separate from death and escape-from-pound subsections.

records.statement: Saturn in twelfth/first when question asked is interpreted as extended time in custody.
preconditions: Conditional long detention, historical claim.

records.statement: Moon in twelfth in conjunction/square/opposition with Mars/Saturn is associated with animal deaths or near starvation.
preconditions: Historic animal-welfare danger claim, not modern veterinary assessment.

records.statement: Heading 'Escape the Pound' begins alternative first-lord and sign modality escape rules.
preconditions: Distinct from general cattle found and pound-location indications.

records.statement: Ascendant lord in movable sign and third/ninth/tenth is described as escaped custody.
preconditions: House-specific condition, no observed animal release.

records.statement: Ascendant lord in twelfth is interpreted as remaining penned, even if otherwise fortunate.
preconditions: Exception to general good-fortune heuristic.

records.statement: Ascendant lord in eighth or principal first significator retrograde is interpreted as animal death while captive.
preconditions: Two historically separate adverse scenarios.

records.statement: Sixth lord in trine/sextile to first lord is interpreted as animal recovered, while square/opposition suggests stoppage.
preconditions: Good vs bad aspects and exact roles must be preserved.

records.statement: Heading 'Whether the Fugitive shall be taken' shifts to person: ascendant lord, Sun and Moon signify querent; seventh/lord fugitive.
preconditions: The historical owner/fugitive relation is not an endorsement or modern policing advice.

records.statement: Ascendant lord applying by conjunction/sextile/trine to seventh ruler or placed in seventh is said to indicate recovering fugitive.
preconditions: Correct direction of first lord to seventh; role and exact aspect types.

records.statement: Seventh lord in first or applying to first, or translation between first/seventh, is another source pathway for more facile recovery.
preconditions: Translation is a separate condition from simple direct placement.

records.statement: The Moon is called natural significatrix of fugitive due to swift motion; Moon in first or favourable to first lord supports return.
preconditions: Historical cosmology, no human tracking.

records.statement: Seventh lord/Moon separating from fortunes then joining infortunes is read as hindrance or capture.
preconditions: Sequential separation and application both required.

records.statement: Moon waxing/light increasing is linked to longer search; Moon waning/decreasing to quicker discovery with less labour.
preconditions: These contrasting timings apply to fugitive recovery, not calendar dates.

records.statement: Moon separating from seventh lord then conjoining first is assigned fugitive regret/returning, with someone interceding.
preconditions: Source inferred feelings are not actual fugitive testimony.

records.statement: Seventh lord combust is interpreted as involuntary capture rather than willing return.
preconditions: Keep distinction between capture and voluntary arrival.

records.statement: Moon's zodiacal quarter indicates direction a fugitive is heading.
preconditions: Separate from planetary house-location map.

records.statement: Seventh lord conjoining an infortune in an angle is said to lead to arrest, while off angle to being detained on the road.
preconditions: Angular vs not changes extent of alleged restraint.

records.statement: First lord aspecting the infortune afflicting fugitive is said to lead to detention by someone demanding money for release.
preconditions: Unverified criminal/ransom allegation; do not advise real detention.

records.statement: Infortune in ninth indicates a person arrested during journey.
preconditions: Only within earlier fugitive-affliction framework.

records.statement: Seventh lord with stationary planet in angle/succedent is interpreted as unable to find direction of flight and later captured.
preconditions: Station type and angularity matters, not all slow planets.

records.statement: Heading 'If a Fugitive shall be found, or come againe' offers voluntary return and forced-recovery alternatives.
preconditions: Separate from capture/detention section above.

records.statement: Seventh lord in ascendant suggests person returns on own accord.
preconditions: Historical author claim only; not validated missing-person outcome.

records.statement: Moon separating from seventh lord, next joining first, is said to produce news or entreaty for fugitive's return.
preconditions: Moon directed aspect timeline different from first lord moving to seventh.

records.statement: Seventh lord combust/entering combustion is said to bring forced return 'volens, nolens'.
preconditions: This is forced/captive return, not consent.

records.statement: Moon next conjoined malefics/retrograde is read as return after suffering misery.
preconditions: No evidence of actual hardship.
